definitions.gloss: invitation letter; written notice; announcement letter
definitions.explanation: A formal written communication inviting someone to an event or informing them of important details such as a meeting, ceremony, or gathering.

examples.japanese: {案内状|あんないじょう}を{送|おく}る。
{案内状|あんないじょう}が{届|とど}いたので、{出席|しゅっせき}の{返事|へんじ}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I received an invitation, so I sent my RSVP.

examples.japanese: {同窓会|どうそうかい}の{案内状|あんないじょう}を{作成|さくせい}して、{卒業生|そつぎょうせい}{全員|ぜんいん}に{発送|はっそう}した。
examples.english: We prepared the class reunion invitation and sent it to all the graduates.

notes:
A compound of {案内|あんない} (guidance, information) and {状|じょう} (letter, document). The suffix ～{状|じょう} is used for formal letters and documents.

USAGE:
Used for formal invitations and notices — weddings, business events, class reunions, ceremonies. Less formal events typically use {招待状|しょうたいじょう} (invitation card) or simply メール or LINE messages. {案内状|あんないじょう} can be informational as well as invitational.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {案内状|あんないじょう}を{送|おく}る — to send an invitation letter
- {案内状|あんないじょう}を{受|う}け{取|と}る — to receive an invitation letter
- {案内状|あんないじょう}を{作成|さくせい}する — to prepare an invitation letter

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {招待状|しょうたいじょう} — invitation card; specifically for inviting guests
- {通知|つうち} — notification; more general, often official
- {挨拶状|あいさつじょう} — greeting letter; for seasonal greetings or announcements
